Native UI lifecycle and skin review: VSUIContext owns the native image provider, UI root, widget defaults, colors, translations and CPU-backed fonts using borrowed viewer settings and LLDir skin/theme/language overlays. Normal native session wiring, required login/status/alerts/agreements and media dependencies, OS DPI/IME and full G-UI/G-RESOURCE closure remain open.

Legacy GTK/LLMOZLIB platform-window API returns GTK layout or NULL, not Vulkan Xlib surface; requires typed export if SDL1 tier supported.
SDL1 shared context methods only warn/return NULL; preserve conditional limitations, do not interpret as native-ready uploads.

Actual constructor only creates headless keyboard; swapBuffers empty. Factory headless mode is not a visible Vulkan window. Diagnostic offscreen target requires its own documented device/no-swapchain contract.
Headless virtual OS/context methods are no-ops/false/null and do not provide WSI. Preserve independently gated headless mode, no inference of a visible native viewer.

init calls selectGLBackend before initWindow, then GL VRAM overrides/info/requirements/driver warnings and self-registered callbacks. Native capability/identity owner must precede callbacks and prevent GL probes; CPU SSE/RAM/input policies remain.

Shutdown stops fetch/cache/decode/thread pools before shutdownGL then viewer window deletion. Native path must cancel/retain producers and drain submitted work before resource/device/window destruction; keyboard remains until views destroyed.

initWindow currently coerces Vulkan to GL, creates LLViewerWindow then pipeline/initGLDefaults with persisted RenderInitError. Replace backend capability/error ownership; preserve startup diagnostics and reference route.

getViewerInfo directly glGetString vendor/renderer/version plus GL VRAM/vendor-based WMI; replace with cached actual Vulkan adapter/driver/backend identity, safe during teardown. CPU/network/library diagnostics remain.
forceErrorDriverCrash calls glDeleteTextures(1,NULL). Legacy crash injection must be gated/disabled/adapted for native backend rather than executing GL with no context.

V4 source review: ordinary native startup enters an owned CPU session before legacy world initialization. Shared default-deny UDP/HTTP admission preserves reliable transport and reviewed handshake/chat/name/mute/alert/logout messages. Weak owners and session generations protect seed, event-poll, name, translation and transfer callbacks; bounded reset/logout paths release partial initialization. Native settings and URL admission prevent deferred world/optional producers; native chat/resources remain on Diligent. Diagnostic replay injects protocol fixtures through the production owner and compares actual connected UI readback with the independent CPU oracle. No graphics/world producer is added. Direct-focus and direct-commit evidence does not establish pointer usability; live authentication remains unqualified.

About reports selected native physical-device device-local heap capacity, counting each heap once including CPU-visible local heaps. It excludes separate host-only heaps, retains unknown when no local capacity is reported, and never queries OpenGL. Memory reporting does not set an allocation budget. Compiler fixtures exercise actual selected-device query/report code and 64-bit sizes; hardware display qualification remains separate. Native About uses selected Vulkan physical device identity: Windows LUID is matched exactly to DXGI adapter and installed package version, without creating a D3D device or GL context. Supplied driver release/build metadata and vendor packing are bounded fallbacks, distinct from API version. Core/extension support is verified before driver-property queries. Production compiler fixtures cover adapter mismatch/retirement and missing metadata; live driver output is separate evidence.
